items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: in the beginning it was Al Boletto with a band out of New Orleans

ctx.x: And you both have been with Louie Bellson on and off — Don for quite a while, right?

My stints were Stan Kenton — I mean in the beginning it was Al Boletto with a band out of New Orleans, and then Maynard Ferguson, Stan Kenton, and then the European thing with the Max Greger Big Band in Munich; and then coming back I went with Buddy Rich and then Louie Bellson and of course Henry Mancini, I worked with Henry for like almost 30 years. But I have to say in all the band leaders that I worked for, Buddy was the one. It’s a great shame I didn’t get to work with Basie. I talked with Basie a couple of…

everybody out of the way and he’d say, “You deal with me, this is my band.” And some of the leaders, and they were all very good, they’d back up and, “It’s your problem, you deal with it, you got it.” Buddy was incredible. He knew exactly what he wanted out of a piece of music, and he’d sit out front, he didn’t read — he had a lot of insecurities and he never gave you that impression by how he played. He had a lot of insecurities. He didn’t read any music. He didn’t know a lot about music, except he knew what was…
